correctness.rationale: For 2<=k<m, the m-eigenspace has 2m-k-2 dimensions and is the kernel of a rank-two matrix whose columns are (1,1),(1,0),(0,1) for M,U,V classes. Minimal coordinate observation is injective exactly when two omitted classes have independent type columns. All other eigenspaces are explicitly detected. For k=m>=3, m and m+2 each have multiplicity m-1 and are detected exactly by one endpoint in m-1 distinct pairs. Counting disjoint allowed configurations yields 2^k*m*(m-k) and m*2^(m-1). Extractable verify.py checks 1094 minimum-size subsets by exact eigenspaces, one full Kalman-rank witness, and a zero-forcing distinction. Finite checks do not replace the general proof.

value.rationale: An all-parameter, exact vertex-level optimum description and count for dedicated control of two communities coupled by k matched bridges is a natural network-design problem. A nontrivial two-constraint column-geometry determines every optimum; the full-matching transition preserves both the minimum budget and exact number of optima while changing their structure. For B_(3,2), the 12 optimum sets include eight that are not zero-forcing, demonstrating why a general strong-structural criterion alone cannot solve the fixed-Laplacian placement question. Not an arbitrary slice or a mere renamed PBH criterion.
